title: Physics‐Informed Meta‐Learning With Graph Attention for Lithium‐Ion Battery Remaining Useful Life Prediction
abstract: ABSTRACT Accurate prediction of lithium‐ion battery (LIB) remaining useful life (RUL) is important for assessing battery degradation and supporting reliable operation of energy systems. However, prediction across different operating conditions remains challenging because of complex spatial–temporal dependencies, limited degradation observations, and difficulties in incorporating degradation‐related physical knowledge. To overcome these challenges, this study presents a physics‐informed meta‐graph attention network (PIMGAN) that integrates degradation feature learning, dynamical regularization, and few‐shot adaptation. Firstly, a multi‐scale graph attention mechanism is combined with adaptive bidirectional temporal convolution to characterize correlations among heterogeneous battery measurements and their temporal evolution. Then, a physics‐guided regulator (PGR) learns a nonlinear differential operator in the latent feature space, whose residual serves as an additional regularization term during model training. Finally, a first‐order meta‐learning strategy is integrated to learn transferable model initialization parameters across multiple degradation tasks, enabling rapid adaptation to unseen battery conditions with limited target‐domain observations while avoiding explicit second‐order meta‐gradient computations. The proposed PIMGAN is evaluated on two publicly available LIB datasets under cross‐cycle and cross‐condition prediction settings. Under cross‐condition evaluation, PIMGAN achieves mean absolute percentage errors of 0.267% and 0.336% on the MIT and XJTU datasets, respectively, demonstrating its effectiveness in battery RUL prediction with limited target‐domain data.
title_zh: Physics‐Informed Meta‐Learning With Graph Attention for Lithium‐Ion Battery Remaining Useful Life Prediction

title: Experimental Investigation For Improvisation Of Soc & Soh Of Battery By Using Ai Embedded Bms In EV
abstract: The research work describes a unified battery management technique that involves a digital twin-based method that encompasses practically validated theory, data-oriented state evaluation, embedded management, and Internet of Things supervision. The task employs two connected phases of experimentation. The first phase consists in the analysis of a six-cell lithium-ion battery pack 3S2P 18650 in twelve operation modes, which consists of using both 0.5C, 1C, and 2C discharges under ambient temperatures of 25°C, 35°C, and 45°C with dynamic loading. The data obtained in the analysis of the voltage, current, temperature, capacity, and energy indicators will serve as calibration data for a second-order Thevenin equivalency circuit digital twin in MATLAB. Phase II benchmarks Random Forest, XGBoost, and LSTM models on 9,742 records from the NASA lithium-ion battery dataset and integrates the selected Random Forest model with an ESP32-based BMS prototype. The embedded platform combines dual INA219 current sensors, a 2-channel relay module, local LCD monitoring, MQTT communication, a Flask-SocketIO dashboard, and a staged voltage-protection strategy. The digital twin reproduces the measured voltage response with RMSE below 0.08 V and R² above 0.98 across the reported constant-current validation cases. In the AI benchmark, Random Forest reaches R² = 0.976, compared with 0.951 for XGBoost and 0.637 for LSTM. Feature-importance analysis identifies current and cycle count as the leading predictors of energy-loss behaviour. Live prototype measurements of 9.87 V, 39.4% SOC, and 100% SOH demonstrate end-to-end sensing, communication, decision, and protection operation. Together, the results establish a practical path from physically validated battery modelling to AI-assisted embedded BMS control.

title: Regime Diagram of Li-Ion Battery Thermal Runaway under Emergency Discharge beyond Exothermicity: Nonmonotonicity and Active Risk Control
abstract: Abstract Thermal runaway (TR) can be triggered in lithium-ion batteries under abuse conditions, leading to significant safety concerns for electric vehicles and energy storage systems. Emergency discharge has been considered as an effective strategy to mitigate TR by reducing the state of charge (SOC), whereas substantial ambiguities remain due to the wide discharge range beyond normal operation and the complex coupling between electrochemistry and TR. In this work, TR experiments are conducted in an Accelerating Rate Calorimeter (ARC) for commercial 18650 LiFePO4 cells, in a range of high discharge temperatures beyond exothermicity (90–110 °C) and discharge C-rates (0.05–18.75 C). Based on the experimental data, a regime diagram is established to isolate TR and No-TR regimes. As discharge temperature increases, the No-TR regime progressively narrows, indicating increasing TR risk. Meanwhile, for a given discharge temperature, increasing discharge C-rate leads to a nonmonotonic system response for TR occurrence, with TR occurrence in the low and high end of discharge rates, yet no-TR in between. Furthermore, the remaining SOC after discharge is nonmonotonic as discharge rate increases, with intermediate C rates achieving the lowest remaining SOC. Based on energy analysis, cells with similar remaining SOC exhibit nearly identical global kinetics regardless of discharge conditions. Statistical analysis reveals that the voltage-drop temperature collected from all the TR tests follows an approximately normal distribution, providing a risk-driven criterion for defining acceptable discharge windows. Measurement using a Simultaneous Thermal Analyzer (STA) has further demonstrated high consistency between the thermal stability of separator meltdown and the voltage drop temperature. These findings not only establish the regime diagram for TR under discharge, but also provide practical guidance for developing effective emergency discharge strategies for TR mitigation.
title_zh: Regime Diagram of Li-Ion Battery Thermal Runaway under Emergency Discharge beyond Exothermicity: Nonmonotonicity and Active Risk Control

title: A Multi-Stage AdSS-NARX-LSTM Approach for Enhanced State-of-Charge Estimation in Lithium-Ion Batteries
abstract: Accurate state of charge (SoC) estimation is essential for the reliable operation, energy management, and safety of lithium-ion batteries in electric vehicles and energy storage systems. However, accurate estimation remains challenging due to battery nonlinearities, measurement uncertainties, and changing operating conditions. This study proposes a hybrid AdSS-NARX-LSTM framework integrating Adaptive State Smoothing (AdSS), Nonlinear Autoregressive with Exogenous Inputs (NARX), and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for SoC estimation. Battery voltage and current are used as primary inputs. The AdSS stage generates a temporally consistent SoC trajectory through an adaptive smoothing process, reducing the influence of measurement noise and short-term signal fluctuations while preserving the overall state evolution trend. In parallel, the NARX model exploits historical input-output relationships to capture nonlinear temporal dynamics associated with battery behavior. The AdSS and NARX outputs are fused with measured variables as auxiliary features before being fed into the LSTM network. This integration enables the LSTM to exploit complementary information while learning long-term temporal dependencies from sequential data. The framework improves estimation stability and robustness without requiring complex electrochemical or equivalent-circuit models. The effectiveness of the proposed method is evaluated using five dynamic driving cycles, including US06, UDDS, LA92, HWFTa, and HWFTb. Estimation performance is assessed using mean absolute error (MAE), mean squared error (MSE), and coefficient of determination (R²) metrics and compared with AdSS, NARX, LSTM, AdSS+LSTM, and NARX+LSTM approaches. Results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves high estimation accuracy and stable performance across different driving profiles, indicating its potential for battery management applications. Further validation, including computational complexity and embedded-system implementation, is required to assess its suitability for real-time operation.
title_zh: A Multi-Stage AdSS-NARX-LSTM Approach for Enhanced State-of-Charge Estimation in Lithium-Ion Batteries
